text: Over the past year, we had also received a large number of high-level incoming visits from state leaders and officials who are keen to engage our agencies, and more so, our economic agencies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These visits provide opportunities to deepen cooperation and build closer economic ties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan had also spoken about our multifaceted relations with Indonesia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both countries are among each other's largest trading partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Such projects and agreements facilitate the creation of jobs and business opportunities on both sides.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: There is still room for us to do so much more together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, discussions are ongoing on ways to expand cooperation in investments, human resource development, infrastructure, tourism and the digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Beyond our close links with the central government, we also have regular high-level visits to Indonesian provinces, and established closer ties with the local leaders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: President Halimah Yacob had a fruitful visit to Yogyakarta during her State Visit in early February.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I visited Riau and Jambi last month, where I met various leaders, including the Riau Governor Syamsuar and the Jambi City Mayor Syarif Fasha.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to engage Indonesia's regions widely to open up opportunities for our businesses while deepening and broadening our people-to-people ties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked how we can deepen our relationship with ASEAN countries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Apart from Malaysia and Indonesia, Singapore continues to closely engage and pursue collaborative relations with the wider Southeast Asian region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have substantive and growing economic, defence and people-to-people ties with many of them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are also exploring cooperation in many new areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With Thailand, we have been exploring FinTech cooperation, like linking PayNow in Singapore with PromptPay in Thailand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This means people in Singapore and Thailand can send money to each other instantly using their mobile phone numbers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have strong economic links with Vietnam, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our seven Vietnam-Singapore Industrial Parks are doing well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Both sides are also strengthening cooperation in finance, digital technology and innovation, smart cities and energy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our agencies, like Infrastructure Asia, are working across the region to support sustainable infrastructure development and share best practices in areas like smart cities, urban mobility and water supply and sanitation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are confident that cooperation in these areas would promote economic growth, social development and long-term stability in our region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I am glad Mr Gan Thiam Poh also mentioned increasing our youth exposure in ASEAN.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With 60% of ASEAN's population below the age of 35, I agree that focus should be placed on strengthening linkages amongst our youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Singapore-ASEAN Youth Fund (SAYF) was set up in 2007 to promote greater interaction amongst ASEAN youths and an increased understanding of ASEAN culture.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our engagement of regional partners also serves as an avenue of cooperation to tackle transboundary threats like cybersecurity, climate change and terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Cybersecurity is a growing concern, particularly for Singapore, which has one of the highest Internet penetration rates in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked how we could work with the international community to safeguard Singapore's cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: MFA works with Cyber Security Agency and international partners to exchange information and promote best practices through active participation in platforms like the UN Group of Government Experts on cybersecurity issues and the UN Open Ended Working Group on Cybersecurity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also launched the ASEAN-Singapore Cybersecurity Centre of Excellence in October 2019, which offers capacity-building programmes for participants.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: According to UN Environment, global temperatures could rise another 3.9°C by the end of the century with catastrophic results.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Although Singapore contributes only to 0.1% of global emissions, we will continue to actively address climate change as a responsible member of the global community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As highlighted by Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean earlier, achieving these goals require deep transformations in our industry, economy and society.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are heartened that there is a growing awareness of climate change among Singaporeans, especially our young.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We look forward to working with the private sector and key stakeholders to achieve our climate goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The terrorist attacks in Sri Lanka, the Philippines, New Zealand and the United Kingdom (UK) last year, as well as the recent attack in Germany, are grim reminders of what is a clear and present danger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In this regard, Mr Liang Eng Hwa raised a pertinent question on how Singapore secured itself from the threat of terrorism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is important that we remain vigilant and continue to deepen counter-terrorism cooperation with our neighbours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We also make use of relevant platforms, such as ASEAN's Our Eyes Initiative for defence officials to exchange strategic information on terrorism, radicalism and violent extremism.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Though further away, our citizens visit the Middle East often, not only for work and education but to perform religious practices like umrah and the haj as well.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the situation and our key engagements there.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The Middle East is an important global supplier of fossil fuels with many key shipping routes passing through the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Any instability in the region will affect Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have thus been closely monitoring developments, which remain volatile.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The dispute between Qatar and its four neighbours, for instance, has persisted for over two years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Singapore has good relations with all the parties involved and we hope that a resolution can be reached soon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Given our position as a major maritime and oil hub, our economic growth could also potentially be impacted if maritime routes are disrupted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The incidents involving Iran and the US in the Strait of Hormuz earlier in January were, therefore, of particular concern given the risk of miscalculations, which could further spiral into conflict and affect regional stability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that all sides will take steps to de-escalate tensions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: No one will gain from a military conflict in the Gulf.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: With regard to the complex and long-standing conflict between the Palestinians and the Israelis, Singapore has taken a consistent and principled position.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We support a negotiated two-state solution consistent with the relevant UN Security Council Resolutions and we welcome all efforts by the international community towards this end.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The US recently released President Trump's vision for a comprehensive peace agreement between Israel and the Palestinians.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: However, this was rejected by the Palestinian side.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We hope that both sides will return to direct negotiations towards a just and durable solution and refrain from any unilateral action.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: While we watch the situation in the Middle East, we have not been deterred from expanding our political and economic space.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have kept up regular interactions with the Middle East at all levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This represented a high-water mark in our relations with the United Arab Emirates, which remains our largest trading partner in the Middle East.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Looking ahead, Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong is scheduled to visit the region to attend the Group of Twenty (G20) Summit later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: These political exchanges lay the groundwork for fostering stronger economic ties with the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our efforts are strengthened by the fact that Singapore is well-regarded in the Middle East as a development model.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They should continue to explore opportunities in the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I conclude by reiterating that we should continue to deepen ties with our closest partners for peace and prosperity of Singapore and the region.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By doing so, we will be better-equipped to secure Singapore's strategic interests in an increasingly uncertain global climate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, I now turn the floor to my colleague, Minister of State Sam Tan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, I shall now elaborate on our relationship with China and our engagement of other key partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Please allow me to do so in Mandarin.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our links with China are long-standing, preceding the establishment of our diplomatic relations, with our founding Prime Minister Lee Kuan Yew visiting China in 1976 and then-Senior Vice Premier Deng Xiaoping visiting Singapore in 1978.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This exchange of high-level visits by our leaders set a strong foundation for our bilateral relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, to Member Sun Xueling's question on the state of Singapore-China relations, we have made good progress in many areas.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat visited China last October in conjunction with the 15th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC), which he co-chaired with the People's Republic of China's (PRC's) Vice Premier Han Zheng.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Recently, Vice Premier Han Zheng suggested to Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat to include cooperation in public health as a new agenda item under the JCBC framework.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore is supportive of this, and we look forward to hosting Vice Premier Han Zheng’s visit to Singapore for the JCBC later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: In addition to JCBC, Singapore will continue to work with China through other high-level platforms, such as the Singapore-China Forum on Leadership and the Singapore-China Social Governance Forum.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, economic cooperation is a key plank of our bilateral relationship.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Apart from our three Government-to-Government projects, we have eight Provincial Business Councils, which facilitate more effective engagement and cooperation with Chinese provinces and municipalities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This brings me to Member Tin Pei Ling's question on how Singapore’s younger leaders will deepen their relations with Chinese leaders over the next few years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat, as well as the Ministers-in-charge of our Government-to-Government projects and Provincial Business Councils, meet their Chinese counterparts regularly to jointly review these projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Many 4G Ministers have also attended high-level events in China and Singapore, through which they built up rapport with Chinese leaders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our 4G leadership will continue to strengthen the friendship and trust between our countries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To Member Sun Xueling's question on the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak on our existing cooperation, while China has borne the brunt of the recent outbreak of COVID-19, Singapore has also been seriously affected by this global health problem.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: International cooperation is crucial to effectively combat COVID-19, a disease which respects no boundaries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: During this crucial juncture, China took decisive measures to prevent further spread of the virus and cooperated with the international community, which allowed the health ministries of many countries, including Singapore, to swiftly develop diagnostic tests and come up with appropriate measures to manage the outbreak together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: China's transparent and sincere actions deserve praise and affirmation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, it is in troubled times that one is tested, and a friend in need is a friend indeed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is vital for us to continue supporting China through these difficult times of combating the virus.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: These proactive fundraising efforts by our people amply demonstrated Singapore's spirit of providing assistance in times of need.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Looking to the future, we will continue to explore and develop new areas of cooperation with China, and leverage new opportunities for our mutual benefit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will also build on high-level exchanges, institutionalised frameworks and concrete cooperation to further broaden and deepen our good bilateral relations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in English.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: It is also critical for us to keep up our engagement of regional and strategic partners outside our immediate neighbourhood.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Allow me to address Miss Cheryl Chan's question on how MFA intends to strengthen our engagement of key partners in the region and also to ensure that Singapore remains a relevant stakeholder.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We had several high-level visits in 2019, including President Halimah Yacob's attendance of the Enthronement Ceremony of Emperor Naruhito and Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong's attendance of the G20 Summit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We look forward to maintaining the positive momentum of our exchanges this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We continue to deepen bilateral cooperation in areas of mutual interest, such as infrastructure cooperation, smart cities and population issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: With the Republic of Korea (ROK), the Prime Minister’s visit last November, in conjunction with the ASEAN-ROK Commemorative Summit, resulted in a number good outcomes in smart cities, IP, cybersecurity and the expansion of Singapore-ROK air services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: India has also one of the largest number of foreign companies in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Our defence ties with Australia are also long-standing.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: This year, we commemorate the 30th anniversary of the Singapore Armed Forces' training at the Shoalwater Bay Training Area in Queensland.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: To assist the Australian Defence Force’s efforts to combat the bushfires in Australia, we deployed two Chinooks to work alongside them for a month.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Singapore and the EU share strong ties and are important economic partners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will continue to deepen our engagement with the EU leadership and also our ties with individual EU member states.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We will also continue to engage the UK post-Brexit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We have many existing bilateral arrangements that will remain in force and we are also working with the UK to ensure continuity by porting over the EUSFTA’s provisions through a Short Form Agreement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: We must continue to strengthen our ties with key partners while expanding our global outreach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
text: Mr Chairman, I shall now turn over the floor to my colleague, Senior Parliamentary Secretary Tan Wu Meng.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Senior Parliamentary Secretary Tan Wu Meng, you have seven minutes.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I take it that you want a little bit more time?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Chairman, Minister of State Sam Tan spoke about how we should strengthen bilateral ties with key partners.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I will share about Singapore's efforts to uphold the rules-based multilateral trading system while playing an active role in international fora.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I will also share how we are engaging our fellow Singaporeans at home and abroad and helping fellow Singaporeans who need help overseas.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked about multilateralism in the present global climate.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Indeed, Sir, trade is Singapore’s lifeline and crucial for our economy.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It is needed to create opportunities for Singaporeans and Singapore businesses.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: By plugging into global value chains, specialising in areas where we have comparative advantage, our companies and workers can upskill, evolve and move up the value chain.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, we have consistently advocated for free and open trade, further regional economic integration and the rules-based multilateral trading system.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We also participate actively and constructively in multilateral fora, such as the World Trade Organization (WTO), Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) and G20.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As convenor of the Global Governance Group, we promote engagement between the G20 and the wider UN membership.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Singapore will continue to play our part to strengthen the foundations that underpin the global trading system.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We are also working with other WTO members to preserve the WTO’s dispute settlement mechanism.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This is crucial for us as it ensures global trade rules are enforced and any trade disagreements, if they happen, are resolved constructively.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Besides the WTO, Singapore continues to pursue bilateral and plurilateral economic agreements to safeguard our economic interests.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: These will create more opportunities for trade and investment beyond Singapore's traditional markets.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: These platforms ensure that the development of international rules and norms reflects the concerns of all countries, big or small.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Singapore has been a strong advocate for small states to play a bigger role at the UN and other multilateral fora.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As Chair of the Forum of Small States, Singapore actively engages fellow small states to discuss common challenges and advance common interests.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have also been contributing actively to the development of international rules.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: For example, we played a key role in shaping what is now known as the Singapore Convention on Mediation, which provides for cross-border enforcement of mediated settlement agreements.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We also participate actively in a UN Intergovernmental Conference to negotiate a new international agreement on the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity of areas beyond national jurisdiction.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And one of our own international law practitioners, Ms Rena Lee, is currently serving as President of this conference.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: For the first time, Sir, Singapore is fielding a candidate to head a major UN body – the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO).

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We are confident that our candidate, Chief Executive of the IP Office of Singapore (IPOS) Mr Daren Tang, has the right credentials to contribute positively to WIPO’s work.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Daren also stands for Singapore’s long-standing commitment to a rules-based multilateral system, international cooperation and inclusive development.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: My colleagues and I wish him the very best at the upcoming elections over the next few days.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We share our development journey with other countries through the Singapore Cooperation Programme (SCP).

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It was established in 1992 for Singapore to "pay forward" the assistance that we received from the international community in our early years of Independence.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Through SCP courses, we support other countries in achieving the UN Sustainable Development Goals and managing global and regional challenges, such as infectious disease control, climate change and cybersecurity.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We will work with our partners to incorporate COVID-19 content into our health-related SCP courses to help strengthen pandemic resilience in the region.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Terence Ho asked about using the arts as soft power.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Indeed, MFA works closely with MCCY to showcase our diverse arts and multicultural heritage overseas.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: MCCY has a cultural MOU with Australia, which has helped many of our performing arts groups presenting works at Australia's major arts festivals.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Many of our overseas Missions also organise cultural events, such as film festivals and art exhibitions, to highlight a softer side of Singapore that people may not always associate us with.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, foreign policy begins at home.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And all of us have a collective stake as external developments can directly affect our future.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We will, therefore, need the understanding of our fellow Singaporeans on our foreign policy decisions, especially when core national interests are at stake.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked about MFA's efforts to engage Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Indeed, we are listening to young Singaporeans' views, ideas and concerns about the world while sharing about the policy challenges and tradeoffs that we face as a small country.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have stepped up sharing sessions with young Singaporeans conducted by our retired experienced MFA ambassadors.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And every Singaporean, by showing the world the best of us and what we stand for, can help grow our space in the world and help keep our little red dot shining.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Your service and dedication help keep Singapore independent and sovereign, and help safeguard the interests of Singapore and our fellow Singaporeans wherever our people may be around the world.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Besides COVID-19, our Overseas Missions also kept close watch on regional developments and provided consular assistance to Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our officers were also on the ground to assist the next-of-kin of two Singaporeans who, unfortunately, lost their lives while kayaking off Mersing, Malaysia, in August 2019.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: MFA will continue doing our best to assist Singaporeans who get into difficult situations overseas.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We also use technology to make consular services more convenient.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our fellow Singaporeans travelling abroad can look forward to a simplified e-Registration process with personal particulars prefilled by MyInfo.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We also accept e-Payments, including PayNow, at our consular service centre and we will continue transforming and digitalising consular and immigration-related services for the public.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Chairman, in conclusion, our foreign policy begins at home.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And MFA, with the support of our fellow Singaporeans, will continue to pursue a foreign policy that serves the interests of Singapore and our fellow Singaporeans amidst an increasingly uncertain global environment.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have a bit of time for clarification.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I fully appreciate his concern for those refugees who are affected.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think the ASEAN Foreign Ministers continue to look at some of these issues and we really want to facilitate the repatriation of the refugees back to where they are.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I just want a little clarification or elaboration on what may happen with Malaysia because, typically, when an administration changes, notwithstanding they may have good relationships with us, they may have different priorities from the previous administration.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: Are there any projects that we think may slow down as a result of that and, if so, what could we do about that?

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The Cabinet in Malaysia has not been announced yet.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: I do not want to prejudge the issue.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: But I will just make two points that we know all the people on the political scene in Malaysia.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: In fact, we have taken extra effort to maintain those links and to build that reservoir of goodwill and trust.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: The second point I want to make is the importance of consistency and a principled foreign policy.

speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
text: So, I hope this is a moment where Singaporeans will appreciate it is good to be boring and consistent.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Otherwise, it is going to be a stalemate.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It would be back and forth and it has been two years since we talked about repatriation and there is still not a single one that is willing to go back.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I think the Member will appreciate that it is not up to ASEAN to allow them to go back.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: It is up to the Myanmar government to allow them to go back.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And really, we want to encourage the stakeholders on the ground to understand such circumstances, especially also the non-government organisations that are working on the ground.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: What we do at the ASEAN level, I can assure the Member, is that at every Foreign Ministers' Meeting, the issue of the Rakhine state will always be discussed.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And whatever the decision that is being made, we have to respect that it is a decision that the Myanmar government will have to take as and when they are ready to facilitate the process.

speaker: The Chairman
text: No one else wants to raise any clarification?

speaker: The Chairman
text: In which case, Mr Vikram Nair, would you like to withdraw the amendment?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: I think MFA is always a very good investment in money.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: It has one of the lowest budgets always and is even lower this year.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: So, a big thank-you to the team serving all across and carrying our flag.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw the amendment.
